measurement_limits: Updates 6..30 are the predeclared timing window; no trimming or stationarity claim.
Native step duration excludes loading, final checkpoint IO and profiling startup; full elapsed time is also retained.
Missing PSS is unknown, never zero; external one-second samples are lower-bound peaks.
No confidence interval or five-percent speed gate is established by a single trial.

Cross-precision timing is descriptive: actual physical-core, SMT and NUMA affinities are not matched by the requested CPU count or CPU model string. Within-arm paired comparisons avoid treating those cross-job placements as equivalent.
Prior quality gate remains unsatisfied; speed evidence does not establish held-out quality.

CUDA allocated-memory benefit is the performance candidate filter. The original design release criterion is at least6GiB lower maximum NVML device-process memory; these are different metrics. Sampled owned-process peaks are lower bounds, and their difference does not bound the true peak difference.
The archived performance protocol's description of its allocator filter as original is not a change to the earlier NVML release criterion; both remain explicitly distinguished here.
Default/legacy v1 portable parity is qualified in the sealed recorded runtime. Historical TF32 settings are not inferred from metadata that did not record them.
